title: Micro-session Transpose Protocol — scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for the "Micro-session Transpose Protocol" (MSTP) — an exploration of a compact API/handshake and on-the-wire format to allow tiny client-side session bundles to be transposed across different runtime backends (hosted, dedicated, private) with minimal coordination.

Motivation / Problem statement:
- Clients (mobile/web/edge) maintain lightweight session state (short history, local embeddings, ephemeral tokens) and need to move that state between endpoints: e.g., local proxy -> hosted endpoint -> dedicated pool
- Current heavy-weight session-offload formats (tarballs, full checkpoint snapshots) are expensive and brittle when latency-sensitive routing and partial-restore semantics are needed
- Aim: define an interoperable minimal payload + small control protocol for partial rehydration, resume fencing, and selective attribute translation (e.g., drop device-only secrets)

Goals / constraints:
- Small: payloads typically <= 4KB for the common case (recent turns + meta)
- Incremental: receiver can accept partial payloads and request missing pieces by id
- Safe: clear trust boundary; client should not be able to escalate privileges by carrying opaque server-side handles
- Versioned: compact version header with graceful fallback to compatible read paths
- Observable: each transpose action emits simple telemetry events (transpose_start, transpose_finish, transpose_partial) with sampling

High-level API shapes (sketch):
1) POST /v1/sessions/transpose 
   Headers: 
     - Authorization: Bearer <client-session-token> (client-scoped)
     - X-MSTP-Version: 1
     - X-Request-Mode: prefer-fast | prefer-complete (hint)
   Body (binary-safe, application/mstp+json or multipart):
     {
       "session_id": "optional-client-id",
       "epochs": [list of per-turn lightweight records],
       "anchors": [ {"type":"embedding_ref","id":"e123"}, ... ],
       "client_metadata": {"device_tz":"PST","capabilities":["local-embed","offload"]},
       "policies": {"drop_pii":true, "max_age_secs":3600},
       "fence_token": "opaque-fence-id-if-present"
     }
   Response: 202 Accepted (async) or 200 with immediate reply if short-circuit
   202 body: {"transpose_id":"t-abc","status":"queued","expected_restore_latency_ms":120} 

2) GET /v1/sessions/transpose/{transpose_id}/status
   - returns progress, missing anchors, or need to fetch from client

Partial restore flow (sequence):
- client -> POST transpose (include anchors referencing large blobs stored locally or via CDN)
- server inspects anchors; if it has them cached it may complete quickly; otherwise it returns status NEED_ANCHOR with list of anchor URLs or anchor_ids
- client may PUT /v1/sessions/transpose/{id}/anchors to supply missing anchor blobs (multi-part upload)
- once satisfied, server returns RESTORE_COMPLETE and issues a session ticket for new runtime handle

Config sketch (runtime side) — single-file flags for testing: 
  mstp.enabled = true
  mstp.max_payload_bytes = 4096
  mstp.partial_timeout_ms = 1500
  mstp.allow_client_anchor_upload = true

Session ticket semantics (short note):
- After successful transpose, server returns a ticket: { ticket_id, valid_until, backend_scope }
- Ticket is ephemeral and scoped: cannot be used to access audit logs or billing-only routes
- Use-case: client receives ticket and can POST to /v1/sessions/{ticket_id}/interact with minimal re-auth

Asciidiagram — rough runtime flow:

Client(local proxy)  --->  Ingress Loadbalancer  --->  MSTP Handler  --->  Cache/Anchor Store  ---> Serving Runtime Pool
       |                          |                        |                         |
       |--POST /transpose (small)---|                        |                         |
       |                          |--inspect anchors------>|                         |
       |                          |                        |--cache hit?-> route to pool|
       |                          |                        |--cache miss-> request anchor |

Design notes / open questions:
- How to represent per-turn provenance compactly? A CRC + short hash might be sufficient for de-dup detection but we should avoid cryptographic ops on hot paths.
- Anchor referencing model: support both content-addressable ids and signed temporary URLs. Need to think about replay risks for signed URLs.
- Fencing semantics: server-issued fence_token must be checked on restore to prevent an older client snapshot from overwriting newer server-side session state. Need TTL and monotonic counter.
- Privacy: by default MSTP should ensure any locally stored PII flagged by policies is not transposed. Add an optional client-level opt-in flag for advanced workflows.
- Cross-backend mapping: some backends have different session attribute models (e.g., kv cache presence). We need a simple translation table or capability flags in the ticket response.

Telemetry / metrics sketch:
- mstp.transpose_requests_total{mode="prefer-fast|prefer-complete"}
- mstp.transpose_success_total
- mstp.transpose_partial_fallback_total
- mstp.anchor_missing_total
- histogram(mstp.transpose_latency_ms)

Failure modes and mitigation:
- Anchor storms: many clients try to upload large anchors simultaneously -> enforce per-tenant anchor upload rate limits and queueing policies
- Malformed small payloads: validate schema strictly and return 4xx with helpful error codes (ERR_MSTP_SCHEMA, ERR_MSTP_VERSION_MISMATCH)
- Partial restore loops: server should cap number of client round trips per transpose (e.g., max_client_roundtrips=3)

Backward compatibility / versioning strategy:
- X-MSTP-Version is the source of truth; server must attempt to accept version-0 and map fields where possible
- For future incompatible changes, return 426 Upgrade Required with info url

Quick experiment plan (local prototyping):
- week 0: rust/python MSTP handler that accepts small JSON bodies, validates, and simulates anchor cache lookup (no real runtime)
- week 1: add anchor PUT endpoint and local file-backed anchor store; measure latency for 512B, 1KB, 4KB payloads
- week 2: integrate with ingress simulator and measure end-to-end (client->transpose->ticket->interact)

Notes / brain dump (incomplete):
- Consider embedding an "effort_hint" in request to let runtime decide to convert to cold-start friendly path
- Might be useful to include a tiny deterministic bloom filter of recent tokens to accelerate de-dup with server KV
- Maybe reuse existing session ticket format (if compatible) to minimize new surface area

Unresolved todos (for me):
- Decide anchor id namespace (tenant-scoped vs global content-addressable)
- Draft error-code enum (numeric + textual)
- Find analogous prior art (some parts similar to "session bundle" used by X internal project) — link GH + JIRA when I find it

References / links to check later:
- GH: redwood-inference/runtime#4721 (early routing/transpose spike)
- JIRA: RINF-2198 (session offload epic)
- Slack: #runtime-arch (thread pinned: "session-offload-strategies")

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally messy — next step is to extract a minimal proto and test flow in a branch.
